title: 1 Samuel Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 12.

questions.question: Who did Samuel say he had made over Israel at their request?
questions.correctAnswer: A king
questions.explanation: Samuel said he had hearkened to their voice and made a king over them, as stated in 1 Samuel 12:1.

questions.question: What did Samuel say about his own age?
questions.correctAnswer: He was old and grayheaded
questions.explanation: Samuel described himself as old and grayheaded in 1 Samuel 12:2, indicating his advanced age.

questions.question: What did Samuel ask the people to witness against him before the LORD?
options: If he had stolen oxen or asses
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Samuel asked if he had taken anyone's ox, ass, defrauded, oppressed, or received bribes, covering all these accusations as per 1 Samuel 12:3.

questions.question: How did the people respond to Samuel's question about wrongdoing?
options: They said he had defrauded them
They said he had oppressed them
They said he had done none of these things
questions.correctAnswer: They said he had done none of these things
questions.explanation: The people answered that Samuel had not defrauded or oppressed them nor taken anything from anyone, as found in 1 Samuel 12:4.

questions.question: Who did Samuel say was witness against the people that they found nothing in his hand?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD and His anointed
questions.explanation: Samuel said the LORD and His anointed were witnesses that they had found nothing in his hand, as stated in 1 Samuel 12:5.

questions.question: According to Samuel, who did the LORD advance and bring up out of Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses and Aaron
questions.explanation: Samuel said the LORD advanced Moses and Aaron and brought their fathers out of Egypt, as in 1 Samuel 12:6.

questions.question: What did Samuel ask the people to do before the LORD to review His righteous acts?
questions.correctAnswer: Stand still
questions.explanation: Samuel asked the people to stand still so he could reason with them before the LORD about His righteous acts, as per 1 Samuel 12:7.

questions.question: Who did the LORD send to bring the Israelites out of Egypt when they cried unto Him?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses and Aaron
questions.explanation: When the Israelites cried to the LORD, He sent Moses and Aaron to bring them out of Egypt as stated in 1 Samuel 12:8.

questions.question: Into whose hands did the LORD sell the Israelites when they forgot Him?
options: Sisera, the Philistines, and the king of Moab
questions.correctAnswer: Sisera, the Philistines, and the king of Moab
questions.explanation: The LORD sold them into the hands of Sisera, captain of Hazor, the Philistines, and the king of Moab, as stated in 1 Samuel 12:9.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel claimed he had received bribes to blind his eyes.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Samuel explicitly denied receiving any bribe to blind his eyes, as he promised to restore anything if taken, according to 1 Samuel 12:3.

questions.question: True or False: The people agreed that Samuel had not defrauded or oppressed them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The people confirmed that Samuel had not defrauded or oppressed them, as stated in 1 Samuel 12:4.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel said he had not walked before the people from his childhood until this day.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Samuel said he had walked before them from childhood until that day, affirming his longstanding leadership, in 1 Samuel 12:2.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel told the people that the LORD was witness against them that they found nothing in his hand.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Samuel declared that the LORD and His anointed were witnesses that they found nothing in his hand, according to 1 Samuel 12:5.

questions.question: Who did the LORD send to deliver Israel from their enemies before they asked for a king?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel
questions.explanation: The LORD sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to deliver Israel, as stated in 1 Samuel 12:11.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 12, which event happened first?
options: The LORD sent thunder and rain
The people asked for a king
The LORD brought the fathers up out of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD brought the fathers up out of Egypt
questions.explanation: The LORD first brought the fathers out of Egypt before the people asked for a king or thunder and rain occurred, as narrated in 1 Samuel 12:6-8.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 12:10, why did the Israelites cry out to the LORD?
options: Because they had sinned and forsaken the LORD
Because they wanted a new king immediately
Because they were hungry and asked for food
Because they wanted to build a temple
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had sinned and forsaken the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:10 states that the people cried unto the LORD, admitting that they had sinned because they had forsaken Him and served Baalim and Ashtaroth, now asking for deliverance.

questions.question: Who were the leaders God sent to deliver Israel from their enemies, as mentioned in 1 Samuel 12:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:11 specifically lists Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel as those whom the LORD sent to deliver Israel from their enemies.

questions.question: What reason did the people give Samuel for wanting a king instead of the LORD as their king in 1 Samuel 12:12?
options: They wanted to be like other nations
They needed a king to fight Nahash, the king of the children of Ammon
They wanted a king to build a palace
They wanted a king to lead religious ceremonies
questions.correctAnswer: They needed a king to fight Nahash, the king of the children of Ammon
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:12 explains the people said 'Nay; but a king shall reign over us' when Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against them, indicating their desire for a king to lead them in battle.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 12:13, who set the king over Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:13 declares that the LORD hath set a king over Israel, even the king whom the people have chosen and desired.

questions.question: What condition is set in 1 Samuel 12:14 for the people and the king to continue following the LORD?
options: Fear the LORD, serve Him, obey His voice, and not rebel against His commandments
Build a temple and offer sacrifices continually
Send offerings to the priests and Levites
Observe all the festivals of Israel without fail
questions.correctAnswer: Fear the LORD, serve Him, obey His voice, and not rebel against His commandments
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:14 clearly states that if the people fear the LORD, serve Him, obey His voice, and do not rebel, then both they and their king will continue following the LORD.

questions.question: What consequence does 1 Samuel 12:15 warn will come if the people do not obey the voice of the LORD?
options: The hand of the LORD will be against them as it was against their fathers
They will be blessed with prosperity and peace
Their enemies will become their servants
questions.correctAnswer: The hand of the LORD will be against them as it was against their fathers
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:15 warns that if the people rebel and disobey, the LORD's hand will be against them just as it was against their ancestors.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 12:16, what does Samuel invite the people to do?
options: Stand and see the great thing the LORD will do before their eyes
Build an altar to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Stand and see the great thing the LORD will do before their eyes
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:16 commands the people to stand and witness the great thing that the LORD will perform before them, setting the stage for a miraculous sign.

questions.question: What sign did Samuel say the LORD would send at wheat harvest, according to 1 Samuel 12:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Thunder and rain
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:17 declares Samuel would call upon the LORD who would send thunder and rain during wheat harvest as a sign of the people's wickedness in asking for a king.

questions.question: What was the people's reaction when the LORD sent thunder and rain as described in 1 Samuel 12:18?
options: They greatly feared the LORD and Samuel
They ignored the sign and continued
They blamed Samuel for the storm
questions.correctAnswer: They greatly feared the LORD and Samuel
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:18 records that all the people greatly feared both the LORD and Samuel after the thunder and rain occurred as a divine sign.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 12:19 show the people's attitude after witnessing the LORD's sign?
options: They asked Samuel to pray for them so they would not die
They declared their innocence and asked for a new king
They decided to rebel against Samuel
questions.correctAnswer: They asked Samuel to pray for them so they would not die
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 12:19, the people beseech Samuel to pray for them that they might live, acknowledging their sin in asking for a king.

questions.question: What advice does Samuel give in 1 Samuel 12:20 to those who have done wickedness?
options: Do not turn aside from following the LORD but serve Him with all your heart
Build a temple to seek forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: Do not turn aside from following the LORD but serve Him with all your heart
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:20 encourages those who committed wickedness to return to wholehearted service to the LORD without turning aside.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 12:21, what will happen if the people turn aside from following the LORD?
options: They will go after vain things which cannot profit nor deliver
They will be protected from enemies
They will prosper in their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: They will go after vain things which cannot profit nor deliver
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:21 warns that turning aside from the LORD leads to pursuing vain things that offer no profit or deliverance.

questions.question: What reason does Samuel give in 1 Samuel 12:22 for the LORD not forsaking His people?
options: Because of His great name's sake and pleasure to make them His people
questions.correctAnswer: Because of His great name's sake and pleasure to make them His people
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:22 states that the LORD will not forsake His people because it pleases Him to make them His people and for the sake of His great name.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 12:23, Samuel would cease to pray for the people because of their wickedness.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:23 explicitly says God forbid Samuel should sin by ceasing to pray for the people; instead, he would teach them the good and right way.

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Samuel 12:14, God promises that if the people fear, serve, and obey Him, both they and their king will continue to follow the LORD their God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:14 promises continuation of following the LORD for both the people and their king if they fear, serve, and obey Him without rebellion.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 12.

questions.question: What did all the people ask Samuel to do in 1 Samuel 12:19 after seeing the thunder and rain?
options: Pray for them that they may not die
Make a new king for them
questions.correctAnswer: Pray for them that they may not die
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 12:19, the people asked Samuel to pray to the LORD on their behalf so that they would not die, acknowledging their sin in asking for a king.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 12:20, what did Samuel instruct the people to do despite their wickedness?
options: Fear not and continue to serve the LORD with all their heart
questions.correctAnswer: Fear not and continue to serve the LORD with all their heart
questions.explanation: Samuel told the people not to fear but to turn back to following the LORD and to serve Him wholeheartedly as stated in 1 Samuel 12:20.

questions.question: What reason does Samuel give in 1 Samuel 12:22 for why the LORD will not forsake His people?
options: Because they promised to obey the king
questions.correctAnswer: For His great name's sake
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:22 explains that the LORD will not forsake His people for the sake of His great name and because it pleased Him to make them His people.

questions.question: What does Samuel promise he will not cease to do for the people according to 1 Samuel 12:23?
questions.correctAnswer: Pray for them
questions.explanation: Samuel states in 1 Samuel 12:23 that he will not sin by ceasing to pray for the people, showing his commitment to intercession.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in 1 Samuel Chapter 12 when Samuel recounts Israel's history and God's faithfulness?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Samuel's speech in 1 Samuel 12 uses inclusio by beginning and ending with God's faithfulness and Israel's need to obey, framing the entire message and emphasizing covenant themes.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word "fear" (yare) as used in 1 Samuel 12:24 in the context of serving the LORD?
options: It denotes reverence and awe combined with obedience
It means to be afraid and flee
It implies submission to human authority
It is used to express anger
questions.correctAnswer: It denotes reverence and awe combined with obedience
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'yare' in 1 Samuel 12:24 means to 'fear' God in a sense of reverence and awe that motivates faithful service and obedience.

questions.question: Which earlier Old Testament deliverers does Samuel mention in 1 Samuel 12:11 as sent by the LORD to deliver Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 12:11, Samuel lists Jerubbaal (Gideon), Bedan, Jephthah, and himself as deliverers God sent to save Israel from enemies.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 12:21, what are 'vain things' that Samuel warns the people not to follow?
options: Things that cannot profit nor deliver
Idols made of wood and stone
questions.correctAnswer: Things that cannot profit nor deliver
questions.explanation: Samuel warns in 1 Samuel 12:21 that turning aside to vain things means pursuing things that cannot profit or deliver, emphasizing the futility of idols or false hopes.

questions.question: What consequence does Samuel warn of in 1 Samuel 12:25 if the people continue to do wickedly?
options: They and their king shall be consumed
They will be exiled to Babylon
They will lose their land to the Philistines
They will have drought and famine
questions.correctAnswer: They and their king shall be consumed
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:25 clearly states that continued wickedness will lead to destruction for both the people and their king.

questions.question: What historical context does Samuel recall in 1 Samuel 12:9 to explain Israel's suffering under foreign enemies?
options: Israel forgot the LORD and was sold into hands of Sisera, the Philistines, and Moab
Israel rebelled against Moses and Aaron
Israel refused to fight the Canaanites
questions.correctAnswer: Israel forgot the LORD and was sold into hands of Sisera, the Philistines, and Moab
questions.explanation: Samuel reminds Israel in 1 Samuel 12:9 that their suffering happened because they forgot God and were oppressed by Sisera, Philistines, and Moabites.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God not forsaking His people as expressed in 1 Samuel 12:22?
options: Romans 11:29 — 'For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance'
Matthew 7:7 — 'Ask, and it shall be given you'
Hebrews 11:1 — 'Faith is the substance of things hoped for'
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 11:29 — 'For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance'
questions.explanation: Romans 11:29 echoes 1 Samuel 12:22 by affirming that God's promises and calling to His people are irrevocable and based on His faithfulness.

questions.question: What does Samuel indicate about his sons in contrast to the king in 1 Samuel 12:2?
options: His sons are with the people but he is old and grayheaded
His sons have already been made priests
His sons will be kings after Saul
His sons are priests serving the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: His sons are with the people but he is old and grayheaded
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 12:2, Samuel contrasts himself as old and grayheaded with his sons who are present among the people, highlighting his long leadership.

questions.question: Which earlier covenant mediator does Samuel mention in 1 Samuel 12:6 as one who was raised by the LORD to lead Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses
questions.explanation: Samuel refers to Moses in 1 Samuel 12:6 as the LORD's appointed leader who brought the Israelites out of Egypt.

questions.question: True or False: In 1 Samuel 12:16-18, Samuel performs a sign involving thunder and rain during the wheat harvest to demonstrate God's power.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: According to 1 Samuel 12:16-18, Samuel calls upon the LORD, who sends thunder and rain at the wheat harvest, a rare event, to show the people their wickedness and God's power.

questions.question: True or False: Samuel tells the people in 1 Samuel 12:25 that if they continue to obey the LORD, both they and their king will be consumed.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 12:25 warns that continued wickedness—not obedience—will cause both the people and their king to be consumed.

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 12:3, what does Samuel challenge the people of Israel to witness against him before the LORD and His anointed?
options: That he has taken no ox or ass, defrauded no one, oppressed no one, nor accepted any bribe
That he has led Israel into idolatry
That he has refused to make a king for Israel
That he has delivered Israel from their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: That he has taken no ox or ass, defrauded no one, oppressed no one, nor accepted any bribe
questions.explanation: Samuel asks the people in 1 Samuel 12:3 to witness that he has not taken any ox or ass, defrauded or oppressed anyone, nor accepted a bribe, thus affirming his integrity before God and the people.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught in 1 Samuel 12:14 about the relationship between obedience to God and the continuation of leadership?
options: Obedience to God ensures the continued reign of both the people and their king
Leadership is independent of the people's obedience
God allows disobedient rulers to reign indefinitely
The people's obedience has no effect on their political stability
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God ensures the continued reign of both the people and their king
questions.explanation: Verse 14 teaches that if the people fear, serve, and obey the LORD, then both they and the king who reigns over them will continue following God, showing a covenantal relationship between obedience and leadership stability.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 12:9-11 illustrate the nature of Israel's sin and God's method of salvation?
options: Israel's forgetfulness of God leads to oppression, but God raises judges to deliver them
Israel's obedience leads to immediate peace without conflict
God punishes Israel eternally without delivering them
Israel never turns away from God and thus never suffers
questions.correctAnswer: Israel's forgetfulness of God leads to oppression, but God raises judges to deliver them
questions.explanation: Verses 9-11 reveal that when Israel forgot God, He allowed oppression by enemies, but when they repented, God sent judges like Jerubbaal and Samuel to deliver them, highlighting God’s justice and mercy in salvation history.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in 1 Samuel 12:22 where it says, 'For the LORD will not forsake his people for his great name's sake'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness and covenantal steadfastness
questions.explanation: Verse 22 emphasizes God's faithfulness, showing that He will not abandon His people because His holy name and covenant require steadfast love and commitment.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 12:12, what reason do the people give for desiring a king instead of God reigning over them directly?
options: They rejected God's direct reign and wanted a human king to lead them
They wanted to worship Baalim and Ashtaroth openly
They sought to return to Egypt
They desired to abolish all leadership
questions.correctAnswer: They rejected God's direct reign and wanted a human king to lead them
questions.explanation: Verse 12 shows the people rejecting the LORD as their king, demanding instead a human king, reflecting a desire for visible human leadership over divine rule.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of the 'king' in 1 Samuel 12:13 being described as 'the LORD hath set a king over you'?
options: God sovereignly permits the establishment of human kingship
The king is equal to God in authority
The king is a false god
The people established the king without God's involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly permits the establishment of human kingship
questions.explanation: Verse 13 teaches that although the people desired a king, ultimately God is sovereign over the appointment of the king, showing His control over political history.

questions.question: Which combined doctrinal truth do 1 Samuel 12:5 and 1 Samuel 12:11 reveal about God's role in leadership and deliverance?
options: God is the ultimate witness and deliverer who raises leaders to save His people
Human leaders act independently from God’s will
Leaders are only accountable to the people and not to God
God abandons His people in times of crisis
questions.correctAnswer: God is the ultimate witness and deliverer who raises leaders to save His people
questions.explanation: Verse 5 confirms that God is witness over Samuel’s integrity, while verse 11 shows God sending judges to deliver Israel, revealing that God sovereignly raises and holds leaders accountable for the salvation of His people.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 12:23 reveal the priestly or prophetic role of Samuel even after the establishment of the monarchy?
options: Samuel commits to continual intercession and teaching the right way
Samuel abandons Israel after the king is appointed
Samuel becomes a military commander only
Samuel declares the end of divine guidance
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel commits to continual intercession and teaching the right way
questions.explanation: Verse 23 shows Samuel’s ongoing role in praying for Israel and teaching them God’s way, indicating the continued necessity of prophetic and priestly ministry under the monarchy.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 12:17-18 demonstrate about God’s control over nature and its purpose in Israel’s covenantal relationship?
options: God sent thunder and rain at harvest to show His power and convict Israel of their sin
Nature is independent of God’s will
God punishes Israel by withholding all rain permanently
Israel controls the weather through rituals
questions.correctAnswer: God sent thunder and rain at harvest to show His power and convict Israel of their sin
questions.explanation: Verses 17-18 describe God sending thunder and rain at an unusual time to demonstrate His sovereign control over nature and to reveal the seriousness of Israel’s sin in asking for a king.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching is found in 1 Samuel 12:20-21 regarding repentance and the futility of idolatry?
options: Repentance leads to serving God wholeheartedly, while idolatry leads to vain and unprofitable things
Idolatry is more profitable than serving God
Repentance is unnecessary if a king reigns
Idolatry is a path to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance leads to serving God wholeheartedly, while idolatry leads to vain and unprofitable things
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 instruct the people to fear and serve the LORD fully, warning against turning aside to vain things which cannot save, thus contrasting repentance with the futility of idolatry.

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized in 1 Samuel 12:6 when Samuel reminds Israel that the LORD advanced Moses and Aaron and brought their fathers out of Egypt?
options: God’s redemptive faithfulness and covenantal faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: God’s redemptive faithfulness and covenantal faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verse 6 highlights God’s faithfulness in redemption history by raising up deliverers and leading Israel out of Egypt, underscoring His covenantal commitment.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 12:25 describe the consequence of persistent wickedness for both the people and their king?
options: Both the people and the king shall be consumed if they persist in wickedness
Only the king will be punished
Persistent wickedness will be ignored by God
questions.correctAnswer: Both the people and the king shall be consumed if they persist in wickedness
questions.explanation: Verse 25 warns that continual wickedness will result in destruction for both the people and their king, emphasizing collective responsibility under God’s judgment.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s allowance of Israel’s demand for a king (1 Samuel 12:12-13) indicates divine weakness or failure. What does 1 Samuel 12:12-13 actually teach about God's sovereignty?
options: God sovereignly permits the people's desire for a king while maintaining ultimate authority
God is powerless to stop the people's demand
God ceases to be Israel’s king
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly permits the people's desire for a king while maintaining ultimate authority
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 show that although Israel demanded a king, God still set the king over them, demonstrating His sovereignty and control over human history despite human rebellion (Psalm 115:3).

questions.question: What does the narrative arc in 1 Samuel 12:8-10 reveal about Israel’s cycle of sin and deliverance in redemptive history?
options: Israel’s forgetfulness of God leads to oppression, and their repentance leads to God’s deliverance through judges
God abandons Israel permanently after sin
Israel’s deliverance is independent of their repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s forgetfulness of God leads to oppression, and their repentance leads to God’s deliverance through judges
questions.explanation: Verses 8-10 recount how Israel’s forsaking God brought oppression, but their cries and repentance resulted in God sending deliverers, highlighting God’s mercy within the covenantal cycle.

questions.question: How do 1 Samuel 12:1-2 and 1 Samuel 12:23 together illustrate the transition of leadership and Samuel's continuing role?
options: Samuel acknowledges the new king but remains a spiritual leader and intercessor for Israel
Samuel rejects the king and leaves Israel
Samuel ceases all involvement with Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel acknowledges the new king but remains a spiritual leader and intercessor for Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 show Samuel presenting the king to Israel, while verse 23 affirms Samuel’s continuing role in prayer and instruction, illustrating continuity of prophetic ministry through political change.
